Vignette

vin-YET · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Vignette is brief evocative story or account.

The novel opens with a quiet vignette of a boy watching the first snow fall outside his grandmother's kitchen window.

Worked Example

The documentary opens with a quiet vignette of an old fisherman mending his nets at dawn.

The scene is short and doesn't advance a full plot, but it captures a mood and a moment vividly -- exactly what defines a vignette.

How Vignette Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

sketch

sketch: a short, simple depiction of a scene or character

snapshot

snapshot: a brief, vivid glimpse of a moment

Antonyms

epic

epic: a long, sweeping story covering great events

How Strong Is It? — anecdote → novel → vignette

anecdote vs. vignette

anecdote vs. vignette: An anecdote is usually a spoken, casual little story; a vignette is more deliberately crafted and often written, aiming for a vivid mood.

novel vs. vignette

novel vs. vignette: A novel takes the idea of storytelling far beyond a vignette, developing full plots and characters across many chapters rather than one brief scene.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — vigne

root — vigne: vine (French)

suffix — -ette

suffix — -ette: small (French)

Put it together

Put it together: Vigne ('vine') plus the diminutive -ette ('small') originally named the small decorative vine-leaf border printed around old book illustrations -- the word grew from 'small vine design' to 'small, decorative scene.'

Use the root in a new word: vintage

Use the root in a new word: vintage: Vintage also traces back to the same vine root, originally referring to the season's grape harvest and the wine made from it.
